saml.description: SAML sources can allow IdP-initiated logins, and the documentation explicitly warns that this may be a security risk because the request is not verified.
saml.note: Do not report acceptance of unsolicited SAML responses as a bug when this option is intentionally enabled.

saml.description: The granted identifier can legitimately change shape depending on the configured/default SAML NameID policy: persistent uses hashed ID, transient uses session ID, emailAddress uses email, and some formats fall back to persistent.
saml.note: Identity mismatches caused solely by NameID policy selection are by design, not principal-collision bugs.

saml.description: Using email-address NameID is supported but discouraged because users may change email addresses.
saml.note: Identity rebinding or merge effects under email-based NameID can be by design.

saml.description: Transient NameID is based on the user's session ID rather than a stable account identifier.
saml.note: Different sessions producing different NameIDs is expected and should not be treated as identity instability.

saml.description: Applications are accessible to all users when no policy/group/user bindings are defined.
saml.note: Broad access with no bindings is documented default behavior and should not be flagged as authorization escalation.

saml.description: If a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, excluding special scopes.
saml.note: Extra claims in userinfo/token under an empty-scope request are by design and should not be treated as over-granting unless explicit minimal scopes were requested.

saml.description: A flow suspended by the Source stage restarts from the beginning if the configured resume timeout is exceeded before return from the external source.
saml.note: This is expected timeout behavior, not a flow-coherence vulnerability.

saml.description: When using a Source stage, the nested source authentication/enrollment flow must not contain a User Login stage or the original flow will not resume.
saml.note: Unexpected direct authentication instead of flow resumption is a documented configuration pitfall, not necessarily a broker coherence bug.

saml.description: Allowing IdP-initiated logins on a SAML source is documented as a security risk because the request is not verified.
saml.note: Acceptance of IdP-initiated login under this setting is by design and should not be reported as a signature-validation bug by itself.

saml.constraint: SAML source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' is explicitly documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. For I1/I3/I5 testing, the fuzzer MUST prefer SP-initiated SAML flows and MUST NOT enable IdP-initiated logins unless it is intentionally testing that insecure mode.

For all SAML tests using authentik as SP, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and then POST the forged SAMLResponse to /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/. The docs define ACS as the assertion consumer endpoint and SAML source flows are SP-driven; sending an unsolicited fabricated response without flow initiation will not correctly bind request state.

For I1 signature-validation tests, configure the SAML source with signed-request/trust settings and a concrete IdP verification certificate/entity configuration. The docs state authentik validates received SAML messages against configured trust material; if the source is left permissive or incomplete, a failed or successful login may reflect setup rather than signature enforcement.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST set a concrete expected IdP issuer/entity ID in the SAML source configuration. If issuer/entity ID is not configured, an issuer-mismatch result cannot be interpreted as a trust-anchor validation failure.

For I2 replay tests, include a control SAML login with a fresh assertion before replaying a fixed_assertion_id. Without a successful control, rejection of the replay attempt cannot be distinguished from generic source misconfiguration or broken flow state.

The Source stage suspends and later resumes the original flow using a dynamic in-memory stage. Any source authentication/enrollment flow used with a Source stage MUST NOT contain a User Login stage, or the source flow will authenticate directly instead of resuming the original flow. This is essential for valid I3 flow-coherence testing.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving stage/policy changes, note that authentik can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid same-request coherence test MUST hold this setting constant; otherwise differences may be by design due to re-evaluation timing rather than a session-binding flaw.

For I3 source-resume tests, the Source stage 'Resume timeout' bounds how long the suspended flow is saved. If this timeout is exceeded, authentik restarts the flow from the beginning on return. The fuzzer MUST keep the external SAML round-trip within the configured resume timeout or treat restart behavior as by design, not a coherence bug.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, compare the same user across password flow and SAML source flow only when both flows are configured to enforce equivalent MFA stages. authentik flows are independently configurable; a missing MFA stage on the SAML path is a configuration difference, not necessarily a protocol bypass.

For I4 identity-binding tests, NameID format materially changes the identifier value. Persistent NameID maps to a hashed ID, transient maps to session ID, emailAddress maps to email, and other formats may fall back to persistent identifiers. The fuzzer MUST keep NameID policy constant across compared logins or it will induce by-design identity changes.

Email-based NameID is documented as unstable because users may change email addresses. For I4 principal-binding tests, the fuzzer SHOULD avoid email-address NameID unless it is explicitly testing email-based merge/collision behavior.

For I4 cross-user collision tests against authentik as SP, do not assume NameID is the binding key. SAML source property mappings can derive user attributes from NameID and assertion content, and source/enrollment flows may link on returned attributes. The fuzzer MUST verify the actual granted identity via /application/o/userinfo/ after SAML login rather than inferring binding from NameID alone.

For I5 audience/conditions tests, authentik as SP consumes assertions at the ACS and SAML security semantics require validation of issuer, audience, and time conditions before session creation. The fuzzer MUST test missing Conditions, missing AudienceRestriction, and wrong Audience as separate cases because a rejection may be due to any one of these checks.

OIDC scope behavior affects post-SAML verification. When no scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. For I5 least-privilege verification using /application/o/userinfo/, the fuzzer MUST request explicit minimal scopes to avoid overbroad claims caused by default scope expansion.

Refresh tokens are not returned unless offline_access is configured and requested. For session-lifecycle tests after SAML-to-OIDC exchange, absence of a refresh token is by design unless offline_access scope mapping is enabled on the provider and requested by the client.

The authorization code can only be used once and expires quickly. For any SAML-upstream-to-OIDC downstream sequence that uses code exchange, the fuzzer MUST not reuse the same code across attempts; a second failure is by design and not evidence of replay protection on the SAML assertion itself.

Token revocation and introspection are provider-scoped. The docs state you can only introspect a token from the same provider used to authenticate, or after exchanging it for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST keep provider/application context aligned when verifying SAML-derived downstream tokens.

SAML source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' is documented as a security risk because the request is not verified and could let an attacker authenticate a user without interaction. For I1/I3/I4/I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST keep this disabled unless it is explicitly testing that insecure mode.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests against authentik as SP, the fuzzer MUST create a SAML Source with signature verification material configured. The docs state authentik validates received SAML messages against its configured verification certificate; without that trust anchor, a failed or skipped check may reflect incomplete setup rather than a vulnerability.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, the fuzzer MUST configure the SAML Source's upstream IdP issuer/entity ID and then vary the assertion Issuer. If issuer/entity ID is not configured in the source, an issuer-mismatch result cannot be interpreted as a trust-binding test.

For I2 replay tests, use SAML assertions against the SAML Source ACS endpoint, not OAuth access tokens. The attack patterns replay_same_token/stateless_jwt_no_jti are not applicable to authentik's documented SAML source flow; assertion replay and OneTimeUse are the relevant SAML freshness tests.

For I2 token-freshness style SAML tests, include a control login with a valid assertion in the same provider/source configuration. Without a control, ACS rejection may be caused by broken source configuration, missing flow state, or signature setup rather than Conditions enforcement.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving Source stage embedding, the source's authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. The docs state this causes the source flow to authenticate directly instead of resuming the original flow, which would invalidate atomicity/coherence conclusions.

For I3 config-change sequences involving flows and policies, distinguish legitimate reconfiguration from incoherent evaluation. authentik documents that flow-stage bindings can evaluate either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run; a valid coherence test must show inconsistent handling of the same request/session, not merely that a later login used updated configuration.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule, MFA enforcement in authentik is flow-based. The fuzzer MUST verify the baseline password flow actually includes Authenticator Validation or equivalent MFA enforcement before comparing it to SAML login; otherwise a missing MFA challenge is not evidence of SAML bypass.

For I4 identity-binding tests, NameID format materially changes the identifier value. The docs state persistent NameID becomes a hashed user ID, transient NameID is based on session ID, email format uses email, and custom NameID mappings may override all of these. The fuzzer MUST hold NameID policy constant across compared logins or it will create false identity-collision/mismatch results.

For I4 email-binding collision tests, avoid configuring email-address NameID unless the test specifically targets email-based binding. The docs explicitly warn that email-based NameID is mutable and not recommended as a stable identifier; using it by default can create by-design merges or rebinding that are not proof of a broker bug.

For I4 cross-protocol or cross-source merge tests, remember that authentik sources can be embedded in Identification stages and may auto-redirect when only one source is configured. The fuzzer MUST ensure it is exercising the intended source path and not an automatic redirect artifact.

For I5 audience/conditions tests on SAML assertions, target the SAML Source ACS endpoint and vary the assertion Conditions/AudienceRestriction. The docs identify the ACS as the SP endpoint that consumes assertions and validates issuer, audience, and time conditions before creating a session; tests against other endpoints are not meaningful.

For I5 authorization-binding tests involving applications, remember that authentik application access is allow-all when no bindings are defined. The fuzzer MUST add explicit policy/group/user bindings when it needs a restrictive baseline; otherwise broad access is by design, not an authorization bypass.

User Login stage numeric sentinel: Session duration default 'seconds=0' means browser-session cookie expiry, not immediate invalidation. Stay signed in offset and Remember device also use duration syntax where values above 0 enable behavior. Never assume 0 disables authentication itself; it selects session-cookie semantics/default no-extension behavior.

Authenticator Validation stage numeric sentinel: Last validation threshold of 0 means MFA is required every time; non-zero relaxes revalidation. For MFA bypass/coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST set this explicitly and not assume 0 means disabled.

Email Authenticator Setup stage numeric sentinel: Token Expiration defaults to 30 minutes. Freshness tests using email-based MFA must account for this stage-specific lifetime rather than assuming immediate expiry or single-use semantics from the API surface.

For SAML signature-validation default tests, create the SAML source with default/minimal configuration and do NOT pre-harden trust settings beyond what the docs require. The docs state authentik as SP supports signed requests and uses configured metadata/certificates; insecure acceptance under default source config is the target of the test, not a setup error.

SAML source 'NameID Policy' controls which upstream identifier authentik uses. The docs state Persistent may be random/hashed, Email address uses email, and Windows/X509 may fall back to persistent. For I4 principal-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST pin the NameID policy deliberately and keep it constant across compared logins; otherwise identity mapping differences may be caused by policy-driven identifier changes rather than a collision bug.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, the docs indicate SAML sources can use Email-address NameID and that email-based identifiers are mutable. The fuzzer MUST test both NameID and email attribute combinations and MUST NOT assume NameID is always the binding key. If email-based NameID is configured, collisions/merges by email may be by configuration rather than a bug.

Email-based NameID is documented as unsafe because users may change email addresses. For I4 tests, any identity merge caused solely by configured email-address NameID should be treated as configuration-driven risk, not automatic proof of a platform bug. Use a control with persistent NameID to distinguish binding policy from unintended collapse.

SAML replay tests must use the same Assertion/@ID across two saml_login events. The docs discuss SAML session tracking and SAML assertions consumed at the ACS. For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, the fuzzer MUST keep fixed_assertion_id identical across both submissions and include a control successful first login; otherwise a second failure cannot be attributed to replay protection.

For I2 freshness tests against SAML assertions, include a control assertion with valid temporal bounds in the same environment. Without a control, rejection of expired/future/no-conditions assertions cannot be distinguished from generic source misconfiguration or broken trust setup.

Source-stage and flow-planning behavior can legitimately change outcomes mid-flow. The docs state stage bindings may be evaluated when planned or when run, and Source stage suspends/resumes flows dynamically. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST show inconsistent handling of the same authentication attempt/session, not merely that an admin changed source/flow configuration between separate logins.

If testing SAML MFA bypass via alternate binding path, note that authentik flows are the enforcement point. A valid I3 test must compare password login flow requiring MFA against SAML source login for the same user under the same effective policies. Do NOT interpret different configured flows as a coherence bug unless the same user should have been subject to the same MFA requirement.

OIDC/OAuth scope behavior affects verification after SAML login if the test uses OAuth endpoints. The docs state that when no scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. For I5 verification using userinfo/introspection, the fuzzer MUST request explicit scopes in control and attack cases; otherwise over-broad claims may be by documented default scope expansion, not an authorization-binding bug.

Refresh tokens are not returned unless offline_access is configured and requested. If a test sequence expects long-lived session artifacts after SAML-to-OIDC style flows, the fuzzer MUST not assume refresh_token presence by default.

User Login stage numeric sentinel: Session duration default 'seconds=0' means session expires on browser close, not an immediately invalid session. Stay signed in offset default 'seconds=0' means no extension prompt. Remember device only activates when duration is above 0. Never interpret 0 as 'disabled validation' or 'zero-second hard expiry' without considering browser cookie behavior.
Email Authenticator Setup stage numeric sentinel: Token Expiration default is 30 minutes. For timing-sensitive tests, configure explicit expiration and do not rely on defaults.

Email stage rate limiting introduces hidden setup limits: Account Recovery Max Attempts within Account Recovery Cache Timeout can block repeated verification emails. If a test sequence triggers multiple recovery/auth emails, the fuzzer MUST account for this rate limit or use fresh identities to avoid false negatives.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
